value.body: Starting work right after Class 12, instead of — or alongside — a degree. There are two broad routes: a salaried entry-level job in the private sector, or working for yourself through a trade, a family business or a small venture. It brings an earlier income and real work experience, while some higher-paying and government posts later ask for a degree or a formal skill certificate.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Suits students who need or want to earn early, who have a family business or trade to join, or who prefer learning on the job. There is no entrance exam: private employers hire through interviews, walk-in drives, job fairs, staffing agencies and job portals, and self-employment needs a skill or idea, some capital and basic registrations.

value.title: At a glance
items: Earning early can matter a lot for family finances and builds work experience before peers.
Entry-level pay is often modest, and many roles are contractual or informal, without PF or ESI cover.
Distance or open-university degrees allow studying while working, which keeps later options open.
Short skill courses — ITI, apprenticeships, polytechnic diplomas — are covered under Vocational / Skilling and can change which jobs are open.
